title: Jobs that make you happy
html:
Stage 1 · Intro

Jobs that make you happy

Talk about jobs — and ask yes/no questions about work.

In other words
How to study — about 25 minutes, top to bottom.
Headphones on. This lesson has real audio — tap ▶ to listen.
After each Check answers, read the note — that is your teacher.

Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

Do you…? Does she…? — yes/no questions about work.
Track 3.5 — questions and short answersOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Do they like their jobs? — Yes, they do. 2 Does he play the piano? — Yes, he does. 3 Does he sell tickets? — No, he doesn't. 4 Do you have a job? — No, I don't.
1Do they like their jobs?
2Does he play the piano?
3Does he sell tickets?
4Do you have a job?
Why

Short answers repeat do/does: Yes, they do · Yes, he does · No, he doesn't · No, I don't.

1Does he play the piano?
2Do you have a job?
Why

Short answers repeat do/does: Yes, he does · No, I don't.

1Does he play the piano?
2Do you have a job?
Why

Short answers repeat do/does: Yes, he does · No, I don't.

In other words
“Does Máté work at the cinema?” — “Yes, he does.”
“Does he always play fast music?” — “No, he doesn't.”
“Do they have unusual jobs?” — “Yes, they do.”
“Do you have a job?” — “No, I don't.”
Notice

Notice: after Does he — is the verb “work” or “works”?

PersonQuestionShort answer
I / you / we / theyDo you have a job?Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
he / she / itDoes he play the piano?Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
careful!no -s after DoesDoes she works? ✗ → Does she work? ✓
In other words
Questions start with Do (I/you/we/they) or Does (he/she/it) + base verb.
The -s lives in Does: “Does she work…?” — never “Does she works”.
Short answers repeat do/does: “Yes, he does.” — not “Yes, he works.”
Jobs take a / an: He's a mechanic. She's an engineer.
Notice

Notice: after Does he — is the verb “work” or “works”? Tell your partner.

In other words
Questions: Do / Does + person + base verb. The -s lives in Does.
Short answers repeat do/does: “Yes, he does.”
Jobs take a / an: He's a mechanic. She's an engineer.
Notice

Notice: after Does he — is the verb “work” or “works”? Tell your teacher.

In other words
Questions: Do / Does + person + base verb. The -s lives in Does.
Short answers repeat do/does: “Yes, he does.”
Jobs take a / an: He's a mechanic. She's an engineer.
Stage 6 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Do or Does?
1___ she work in a hospital?
2___ you earn a good salary?
3___ your brother enjoy his job?
4___ they work full-time?
5Does he work from home? — Yes, he ___.
6Do you like Mondays? — No, I ___.
Why

she / your brother → Does; you / they → Do. Short answers: Yes, he does · No, I don't.

1❌ “Does she works in a bank?”
2❌ “Do he have a boss?”
3❌ “Yes, she do.”
Why

Does she work · Does he have · Yes, she does.

1He's ___ engineer.
2She's ___ nurse.
3I ___ work at weekends.
4He ___ earn much, but he loves the work.
Why

an + vowel sound (an engineer) · a nurse · I don't · he doesn't.

1___ your mother work full-time?
2___ your friends like their jobs?
3Does she enjoy Mondays? — No, she ___.
4Do they work from home? — Yes, they ___.
Why

your mother → Does; your friends → Do. Short answers repeat do/does.

1❌ “Does he plays the guitar?”
2❌ “Do she work part-time?”
3❌ “Yes, they does.”
Why

Does he play · Does she work · Yes, they do.

1She's ___ engineer.
2He's ___ pilot.
3We ___ work on Sundays.
Why

an engineer · a pilot · we don't.

1___ your mother work full-time?
2___ your friends like their jobs?
3Does she enjoy Mondays? — No, she ___.
4Do they work from home? — Yes, they ___.
Why

your mother → Does; your friends → Do. Short answers repeat do/does.

1❌ “Does he plays the guitar?”
2❌ “Do she work part-time?”
3❌ “Yes, they does.”
Why

Does he play · Does she work · Yes, they do.

1She's ___ engineer.
2He's ___ pilot.
3We ___ work on Sundays.
Why

an engineer · a pilot · we don't.

Stage 7 · Read

Read

Two people who smile on Monday morning.
1Why are Asel and Marco happy at work?
Why

Happy workers don't always earn the most — they enjoy their work.

1Asel works freelance, from home.
2Asel has a boss.
3Marco works short hours.
4The kitchen is often stressful.
5Happy workers always earn the most money.
Why

Asel doesn't have a boss. Marco works long hours. Happy workers don't always earn the most.

1Asel asks: “Does a big office ___ you happy?”
2“She's ___ photographer.”
3Find the word that means “people you work with”.
Why

Does + base verb: make · a photographer · colleagues = people you work with.

1What is Asel's job?
2Why doesn't Asel have a boss?
3Who are Marco's “second family”?
4What is the secret of happy workers?
Why

Asel — a freelance photographer, no boss. Marco's colleagues are his second family. The secret: they enjoy their work.

1Marco asks: “___ your job do that?”
2“He's ___ chef.”
Why

Does your job… · a chef.

Stage 8 · Listen

Listen

Track 3.3 — the piano player and the fire lookoutOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
M: I work at a cinema in town, but I don't sell tickets, I'm the piano player! At my cinema they have a lot of old, silent movies so they need someone to play music. I watch the film and decide what type of music to play. If it's a sad part of the film, I play slow music; but if it's an exciting part, I play it fast. — D: I am a 'fire lookout' and I work in a big forest. Fire can be very dangerous here, so my job is to make sure no fires start. I work in a very high tower, so I can see very far. I check the weather on the internet every morning. I like my job because the forest is beautiful and quiet.
Two very unusual jobs.

Listen once. Then answer with short answers.

1Does Máté sell tickets at the cinema?
2Does he always play fast music?
3Does Dana work in a big office?
4Does she enjoy her job?
Why

He doesn't sell tickets — he plays for silent films, slow OR fast. Dana works in a tower and loves the quiet forest.

Two very unusual jobs.

Listen once. Then answer.

1Where does Máté work?
2Where does Dana work?
3Does Dana like her job?
Why

Máté plays piano at a cinema · Dana watches for fires from a tower — and loves the quiet forest.

Stage 9 · Write

Write

Write about your job — or your dream job.

5–6 sentences. Use a/an, and one don't/doesn't sentence.

Useful language
  • I'm a… / I want to be a…
  • I work / I don't work…
  • full-time · part-time · freelance
  • My colleagues are…
  • The salary is…
  • I enjoy…
Guess the job — yes/no questions only.

Think of a job. Your partner asks questions and guesses.

Useful language
  • Does he / she work…?
  • Does she wear a uniform?
  • Does he earn a lot?
  • Yes, she does.
  • No, he doesn't.
  • Is it a…?
Guess the job — yes/no questions only.

Think of a job. Your teacher asks questions and guesses.

Useful language
  • Does he / she work…?
  • Does she wear a uniform?
  • Does he earn a lot?
  • Yes, she does.
  • No, he doesn't.
  • Is it a…?
In other words
Step 1 — think of a job (from this lesson or any job you know).
Step 2 — your partner asks ONLY yes/no questions: “Does she work outside? Does he wear a uniform? Does she earn a lot?” You answer: “Yes, she does. / No, he doesn't.”
Step 3 — they guess: “Is it a pilot?” Then swap. Three rounds each.

Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1___ she work at night?
2___ they like the job?
3He ___ wear a uniform. (negative)
Why

Does + he/she/it \u00b7 Do + I/you/we/they \u00b7 short answer: No, he doesn't.

1Do she work here?
2Does they like the job?
3He don't wear a uniform.
Why

Does + he/she/it \u00b7 Do + I/you/we/they \u00b7 short answer: No, he doesn't.

1Make a question: She works at night.
2Make a question: They earn a good salary.
3Answer with NO: Does he travel a lot?
Why

Does + he/she/it \u00b7 Do + I/you/we/they \u00b7 short answer: No, he doesn't.
